In this path, jsoup was only using available() as a hint to speed optimize charset detection, so that exception was too strong a signal... I found this while chasing a flaky ConnectTest.maxBodySize failure on JDK 8 Ubuntu CI. The stack ended up in charset sniffing, and the exception was coming from InputStream.available(), not from an actual body read.' No verbatim stack-trace text was quoted in the issue body (commentCount: 0, no discussion thread). Diff-confirmed at both touched files: SimpleBufferedInput.fill() previously called `if (in.available() < 1) break;` unguarded inside its opportunistic-refill loop; the fix wraps it in try/catch(IOException), breaking (and keeping already-buffered bytes) instead of letting the IOException propagate. SimpleStreamReader.read(char[],int,int) previously called `!(in.available() > 0)` unguarded inline in its decode-underflow branch; the fix extracts this into a new private hasAvailableBytes() that catches IOException and returns false. findings.claim: {"class":"CRASH_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION","secondary":["RESOURCE_LEAK"],"description":"Commit message: 'Apply the default 512 max stack depth to the XML parser (#2570)'. No linked issue and no separate reporter narrative -- forge_issue(2570) resolves to the PR itself with an empty body. Diff-confirmed: at the parent commit, XmlTreeBuilder overrode `int defaultMaxDepth()` to return `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, i.e. effectively unbounded recursion/stack growth for deeply nested XML input, unlike the HTML tree builder which uses TreeBuilder's bounded default.
